title: Logical BRAINK computer identity survives physical host migration
classification: logical computer identity / migration / semantic virtualization
statement: A logical BRAINK computer identity and its required persistent state can be reconstructed on a different physical host without redefining that logical identity.
invariants: logical computer identifier is independent of hostname, machine-id, IP address and transport endpoint
required persistent state is preserved across host replacement
carrier-specific identifiers remain projections rather than logical identity
state transfer is performed through the governed KEX mirror/update lane rather than a duplicate BRAINK copy mechanism

falsification.experiment: Instantiate a logical computer on host A, persist its governed R26/R31 state, create a verified KEX mirror package, restore it on independent host B through the same mirror runtime, and verify the same logical identifier, state digest, lineage and authority while machine/transport identifiers differ.
falsification.pass_condition: Host A and host B present the same logical computer identity and required state/authority invariants while exposing different machine/carrier identities and matching verified mirror update/restore manifest digests.
falsification.fail_condition: Logical identity changes with hostname/machine-id/IP, required state cannot be reconstructed, mirror parity fails, or authority/lineage diverges.

proof_requirements.description: Exercise logical identity and governed KEX mirror update/restore on one executor without claiming cross-machine proof.
Capture logical identity, R26/R31 state, lineage, authority and verified KEX mirror manifest on host A.
Reconstruct the same logical computer on independent host B through the governed mirror restore runtime.
External consumer resolves and interacts with the logical identity after migration.
Repeat migration/rehydration without logical identity drift.

invalid_overclaims: Current remote_fabric_node node_id is not proof of this claim because it includes machine_material().
A same-host process restart is not cross-host migration.
A same-executor mirror restore is integration evidence only.
A carrier endpoint change is not physical-host replacement.
Queued independent-host CI is not cross-machine evidence.
A verified mirror receipt proves transfer parity, not BRAINK logical identity invariance by itself.
next_experiments: Execute governed L5 integration lane on an available executor.
Execute Host A L7 baseline on a distinct resident executor.
Execute Host B L9 rehydration on a distinct resident executor.
Repeat A-to-B and B-to-A migrations for L11 repeatability evidence.
